newsitem.title: UK: CE Electric rejects N.Electric claim on value.
newsitem.headline: CE Electric rejects N.Electric claim on value.

text.p: CE Electric, which has bid 630 pence per share for Northern Electric, said it had "at no time" suggested any intent to value the company at around 700 pence per share, "or even anywhere close to this figure."
"This range was entirely the proposal of Northern Electric," a spokesman said on Monday.

The spokesman added that CE Electric, which is 70 percent owned by U.S.-based CalEnergy, said Northern Electric had said financial information would be made available "to substantiate such an ambition."
"Because we don't believe that such "remarkable' information is available, we regard Northern Electric's associated negotiating position as unrealistic," the spokesman said.
He added that CE Electric had decided to let shareholders assess for themselves the value of ordinary shares.
CE Electric added that it believed the terms of its offer "represent full and fair value."

CE Electric, in which U.S.-based construction, mining and telecoms group Peter Kiewit has a 30 percent stake, launched the hostile $1.225 billion on Monday and swept up a 12.72 percent stake in Northern Electric.
The regional electricity company rejected the bid, claiming that it had received a proposal at 700 pence per share in the culmination of talks on Sunday.
